source: English seeds translated to Japanese with verbal collocation analysis

translations.english: I want to speak Spanish with you now.
translations.japanese: 今あなたと日本語を話したいです。
translations.notes: want to + verb becomes verb-stem + たい in Japanese. Two English verbs collapse into one Japanese form.

translations.english: I'm trying to learn.
translations.japanese: 勉強しようとしています。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 勉強しようとしている
translations.notes: trying to + verb becomes volitional + としている. Progressive in both languages.

translations.english: how to speak as often as possible
translations.japanese: できるだけ頻繁に話す方法
translations.notes: how to + verb becomes verb + 方法 (method/way). Fragment, not full sentence.

translations.english: how to say something in Spanish
translations.japanese: 日本語で何かを言う方法
translations.notes: how to + verb becomes verb + 方法. Fragment.

translations.english: I'm going to practise speaking with someone else.
translations.japanese: 他の人と話す練習をするつもりです。
translations.notes: going to becomes つもり (intention). practise + verb-ing becomes verb + 練習.

translations.english: I'm trying to recall a word.
translations.english_canonical: I'm trying to remember a word.
translations.japanese: 言葉を思い出そうとしています。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 思い出そうとしている
translations.notes: JPN_FOR_ENG: Changed 'remember' to 'recall' to disambiguate from 覚える (retain). 思い出す = retrieve from memory.

translations.english: I want to try as hard as I can today.
translations.japanese: 今日はできるだけ頑張りたいです。
translations.notes: want to try collapses to 頑張りたい. 'as hard as I can' becomes できるだけ.

translations.english: I'm going to try to explain what I mean.
translations.japanese: 言いたいことを説明しようとするつもりです。
translations.notes: Complex stacking: going to try to explain. Multiple verbal collocations.

translations.english: I speak a little Spanish now.
translations.japanese: 今は日本語を少し話します。
translations.notes: Simple present tense. No verbal collocations.

translations.english: I'm not sure if I can remember the whole sentence.
translations.japanese: 文全体を覚えられるかどうかわかりません。
translations.notes: can + verb becomes potential form (られる/える). I'm not sure becomes わかりません.

translations.english: I'd like to be able to speak after you finish.
translations.japanese: あなたが終わった後に話せるようになりたいです。
translations.notes: would like to becomes たい. be able to speak becomes 話せるようになる (become able to speak).

translations.english: I wouldn't like to guess what's going to happen tomorrow.
translations.japanese: 明日何が起こるか推測したくないです。
translations.notes: wouldn't like to becomes たくない. going to happen becomes just 起こる (future implied by context).

translations.english: You speak Spanish very well.
translations.japanese: あなたは日本語をとても上手に話します。
translations.notes: Simple present. No verbal collocations.

translations.english: Do you speak Spanish all day?
translations.japanese: 一日中日本語を話しますか？
translations.notes: Simple question. No verbal collocations.

translations.english: And I want you to speak Spanish with me tomorrow.
translations.japanese: そして明日、あなたに私と日本語を話してほしいです。
translations.notes: want someone to do = てほしい. Different from wanting to do something yourself (たい).

translations.english: He wants to come back with everyone else later on.
translations.japanese: 彼は後でみんなと一緒に戻りたいです。
translations.notes: want to + verb becomes verb-stem + たい. come back = 戻る.

translations.english: She wants to find out what the answer is.
translations.japanese: 彼女は答えが何かを知りたいです。
translations.notes: want to find out = 知りたい. Phrasal verb 'find out' becomes simple 知る.

translations.english: We want to meet at six o'clock this evening.
translations.japanese: 私たちは今晩6時に会いたいです。
translations.notes: want to + verb becomes verb-stem + たい.

translations.english: But I don't want to stop talking.
translations.japanese: でも話すのをやめたくないです。
translations.notes: don't want to becomes たくない. stop + verb-ing becomes verb + のをやめる.

translations.english: You want to learn his name quickly.
translations.japanese: あなたは彼の名前を早く覚えたいです。
translations.notes: want to learn = 覚えたい. 'learn' as in memorize = 覚える (different from 勉強する).

translations.english: Why are you learning her name?
translations.japanese: なぜ彼女の名前を覚えているんですか？
translations.notes: Progressive 'learning' becomes 覚えている. No verbal collocations.

translations.english: Because I want to meet people who speak Spanish.
translations.japanese: 日本語を話す人に会いたいからです。
translations.notes: want to meet = 会いたい. 'people who speak' = 話す人 (relative clause).

translations.english: I'm going to start talking more soon.
translations.japanese: もうすぐもっと話し始めるつもりです。
translations.notes: going to = つもり. start + verb-ing becomes verb-stem + 始める.

translations.english: I'm not going to be able to remember easily.
translations.japanese: 簡単に覚えられないでしょう。
translations.notes: going to be able to remember = 覚えられないでしょう. Complex English structure simplifies in Japanese.

translations.english: Are you going to help me before I have to go?
translations.japanese: 私が行かなければならない前に手伝ってくれますか？
verbal_collocations_japanese: 行かなければならない
translations.notes: have to = なければならない. going to (future) becomes simple present in Japanese question.

translations.english: I like feeling as if I'm nearly ready to go.
translations.japanese: もうすぐ行く準備ができているような気持ちが好きです。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 行く準備ができている
translations.notes: like + verb-ing = verb + のが好き. ready to go = 行く準備ができている.

translations.english: I don't like taking too much time to answer.
translations.japanese: 答えるのに時間をかけすぎるのは好きじゃないです。
translations.notes: don't like + verb-ing = verb + のは好きじゃない.

translations.english: It's useful to start talking as soon as you can.
translations.japanese: できるだけ早く話し始めることは役に立ちます。
translations.notes: It's useful to = verb + ことは役に立つ. start talking = 話し始める.

translations.english: I'm looking forward to speaking better as soon as I can.
translations.japanese: できるだけ早くもっと上手に話せるようになるのを楽しみにしています。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 話せるようになるのを楽しみにしている
translations.notes: looking forward to = のを楽しみにしている. speaking better = もっと上手に話せるようになる.

translations.english: I wanted to ask you something yesterday.
translations.japanese: 昨日あなたに何か聞きたかったです。
translations.notes: wanted to = たかった (past tense of たい).

translations.english: You wanted to speak with me tonight.
translations.japanese: あなたは今夜私と話したかったです。
translations.notes: wanted to speak = 話したかった.

translations.english: Did you want to show me something?
translations.japanese: 何か見せたかったんですか？
translations.notes: Did you want to = たかったんですか. Polite past question.

translations.english: How long have you been learning Spanish?
translations.japanese: どのくらい日本語を勉強していますか？
translations.notes: have been + verb-ing becomes ている form. Duration + ている.

translations.english: He doesn't want to be quiet when other people are here.
translations.japanese: 他の人がいる時、彼は静かにしたくないです。
translations.notes: doesn't want to be quiet = 静かにしたくない.

translations.english: She doesn't want to read anything this afternoon.
translations.japanese: 彼女は今日の午後何も読みたくないです。
translations.notes: doesn't want to read = 読みたくない.

translations.english: We don't want to interrupt the story.
translations.japanese: 私たちは話を邪魔したくないです。
translations.notes: don't want to interrupt = 邪魔したくない.

translations.english: I started to think about it carefully last month.
translations.japanese: 先月からそれについてよく考え始めました。
translations.notes: started to think = 考え始めた. verb-stem + 始める pattern.

translations.english: I've been learning for about a week.
translations.japanese: だいたい一週間勉強しています。
translations.notes: have been + verb-ing = ている. Duration expression with ている.

translations.english: But I'm a little tired this morning.
translations.japanese: でも今朝は少し疲れています。
translations.notes: am tired = 疲れている. State verb in Japanese.

translations.english: How do you feel at the moment?
translations.japanese: 今どう感じていますか？
translations.notes: Simple question about feeling. No verbal collocations.

translations.english: I feel okay, but I'm starting to feel tired.
translations.japanese: 大丈夫ですが、疲れ始めています。
translations.notes: starting to feel = 始めている. verb-stem + 始める.

translations.english: I was starting to feel better than last night.
translations.japanese: 昨夜よりも気分が良くなり始めていました。
translations.notes: was starting to feel = 始めていました (past progressive).

translations.english: I wasn't thinking about how to answer.
translations.japanese: どう答えるか考えていませんでした。
translations.notes: how to answer = どう答えるか. wasn't thinking = 考えていなかった.

translations.english: Or if I need to improve.
translations.japanese: または上達する必要があるかどうか。
translations.notes: need to = 必要がある. Fragment.

translations.english: I don't need to know everything.
translations.japanese: 全部を知る必要はないです。
translations.notes: don't need to = 必要はない.

translations.english: But I don't worry about making mistakes.
translations.japanese: でも間違えることを心配しません。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 間違えることを心配する
translations.notes: worry about + verb-ing = verb + ことを心配する.

translations.english: Because I think that it's a good thing to make mistakes.
translations.japanese: 間違えることは良いことだと思うからです。
translations.notes: to make mistakes = 間違えること (nominalized verb).

translations.english: I don't care about making mistakes.
translations.japanese: 間違えることは気にしません。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 間違えることを気にする
translations.notes: don't care about + verb-ing = verb + ことは気にしない.

translations.english: It's like this, if you know what I mean.
translations.japanese: こういう感じです、言いたいことがわかれば。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 言いたいことがわかる
translations.notes: what I mean = 言いたいこと. Idiomatic expression.

translations.english: I'm not trying to finish as quickly as possible.
translations.japanese: できるだけ早く終わらせようとしているわけではないです。
verbal_collocations_japanese: 終わらせようとしている
translations.notes: not trying to = しようとしているわけではない. Emphasis on negation.

verb_inventory.want: たい (suffix attached to verb stem)
verb_inventory.learn (study): 勉強する / 勉強します
verb_inventory.try: しようとする (volitional + to suru)
verb_inventory.practise: 練習する / 練習します
verb_inventory.explain: 説明する / 説明します
verb_inventory.can: できる / られる/える
verb_inventory.guess: 推測する / 推測します
verb_inventory.happen: 起こる / 起こります
verb_inventory.have to: なければならない / ないといけない
verb_inventory.mean: 言いたいこと / 意味する
verb_inventory.finish: 終わる / 終わらせる

english_to_japanese_mappings.have to + verb: verb + なければならない
english_to_japanese_mappings.look forward to + verb-ing: verb + のを楽しみにしている
english_to_japanese_mappings.how to + verb: verb + 方法 / どう + verb + か

master_keys_japanese.description: Japanese patterns that cover multiple English forms

たい_suffix.example: 話したい (want to speak), 話したかった (wanted to speak)

volitional_to_shiteiru.example: 話そうとしている (trying to speak)

potential_form.example: 話せる (can speak), 話せた (could speak)

te_form_hoshii.example: 話してほしい (want you to speak)

key_observations: Japanese collapses 'want to + verb' into single たい suffix - major simplification
English 'trying to' requires volitional form + としている in Japanese
English progressive 'am/is/are + verb-ing' often maps to ている form
Japanese potential form (られる/える) covers 'can', 'be able to', 'could'
'start + verb-ing' becomes verb-stem + 始める - elegant compound verb
Negation patterns: たくない (don't want to), なければならない (have to), 必要はない (don't need to)
cognitive_load_notes: Japanese verb forms change more than English (conjugation complexity)
But Japanese has fewer DISTINCT auxiliary patterns than English
Master keys: たい, potential form, ている, なければならない cover many English patterns
